title: aspect-ratio and object-fit
summary: Keep media at the right shape without stretching it.
nestedConcepts: Choose how an image fills its frame

subtopics.title: aspect-ratio
subtopics.explanation: `aspect-ratio` describes the width-to-height relationship of a box, such as `16 / 9`. The browser can reserve that shape before an image finishes loading, which reduces layout jumps. It is like choosing a picture frame before printing the photo. Apply it to a media wrapper and check it at narrow widths.

subtopics.title: object-fit:
subtopics.explanation: `object-fit: cover` fills the image box while keeping the source proportions, so some edges may be cropped. It is like trimming a photo to fill a frame. This works for uniform thumbnails, but inspect the crop so a face, label, or important object is not cut off.

subtopics.title: object-fit:
subtopics.explanation: `object-fit: contain` keeps the full image visible inside its box, though empty space may remain around it. It is like shrinking a poster to fit a frame without cutting its text. Use it for product diagrams, logos, and screenshots where every edge matters.

subtopics.title: object-position
subtopics.explanation: `object-position` moves the visible part of an image when the box crops it. For example, `object-position: center top` keeps more of the upper area in view. It is like sliding a photo behind a fixed window. Choose a focal point that keeps useful context visible.

subtopics.title: Write useful alternative text
subtopics.explanation: Alternative text tells people using screen readers what an informative image contributes. Decorative images can use empty alt text so they are skipped. Cropping and alternative text solve different problems: keep important visual content visible, and provide a text equivalent when the image carries meaning. Alt text is like a caption explaining why the picture matters.

foundations.overview: Images and videos often arrive in different shapes, but a layout may need a predictable space. `aspect-ratio` sets the shape of that space. `object-fit` decides how the media fills it. Think of placing a photo in a frame: you can crop the edges or shrink the whole photo to keep everything visible. Add useful alternative text when an image carries information.
foundations.whyItMatters: Media dimensions affect layout stability and whether a visual remains useful after cropping. Separate box shape, fit behavior, focal position, and text alternatives.
foundations.realWorldUsage: A photo frame can crop a picture or show the whole picture with margins.
commonUseCases: Reserve space for video thumbnails in a responsive card grid.
Crop profile photos consistently without distorting them.
Keep a product diagram fully visible inside a fixed-size panel.
Reserve a consistent frame for video cards while thumbnails load.
Keep product packaging fully visible with contain inside a fixed panel.
Crop profile pictures uniformly while keeping a person’s face in view.
Keep a logo fully visible with contain rather than cropping its edges.
Use cover for a profile tile only after checking the subject remains visible.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Aspect ratio guarantees the source image has that shape.
commonMisconceptions.reality: It controls the element box; object-fit decides how a differently shaped source is displayed.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Cover is always the best option because it fills the card.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Cover can remove meaningful content, so choose contain or a different crop when detail matters.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Aspect ratio changes the source image itself.
commonMisconceptions.reality: It sets a preferred box shape; object-fit controls how a differently shaped source appears.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Cover preserves every edge of a photo.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Cover fills the box by cropping edges when source and box ratios differ.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Alternative text can compensate for a poor crop.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Alt text provides a text equivalent; it does not make an important visual detail visible.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Changing object-fit changes an image’s alternative text.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Fit controls visual rendering; alternative text is separate information for nonvisual access.

keyTakeaways: `aspect-ratio` describes the width-to-height relationship of a box, such as `16 / 9`.
`object-fit: cover` fills the image box while keeping the source proportions, so some edges may be cropped.
`object-fit: contain` keeps the full image visible inside its box, though empty space may remain around it.
`object-position` moves the visible part of an image when the box crops it.
Alternative text tells people using screen readers what an informative image contributes.

codeLab.expectedOutput: The preview demonstrates the CSS behavior described in the task.
